title: Lead-CPR: Psychological effects of shared team leadership during cardiopulmonary resuscitation – a prospective randomised simulation study
summary: A rapid and well-coordinated response is essential during cardiopulmonary resuscitation. A resuscitation team is usually led by one person who coordinates and oversees all measures. Having to manage several tasks at once can place a high workload on the team leader. The study examines whether sharing formal leadership responsibilities between two people influences psychological processes during cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Physicians complete the same simulated scenario with either single or shared leadership. They then answer questions electronically about their workload, teamwork and information from the scenario.

interventions.name: Control group: Simulated resuscitation of a patient with ventricular fibrillation. A single team leader is responsible for coordinating all resuscitation measures.

Intervention group: Simulated resuscitation of a patient with ventricular fibrillation. Leadership responsibilities are shared by two designated team leaders with equal authority and predefined areas of responsibility.
